title: GPU pool utilization walkthrough and rate experiments
content:
Purpose:
This is a working spreadsheet-style walkthrough + experimental notes for modeling reserved GPU pool economics and potential rate constructs. Goal: produce a simple, explainable mapping from reserved commit (monthly GPU capacity) -> effective per-GPU-hour and per-token cost under different utilization smoothing strategies, and then derive candidate customer-facing pricing tiers and overage rules.

Audience:
Product pricing, sales engineer, finance modeling, solutions engineering. Not final — contains assumptions and TODOs.

High-level summary (one-liner):
- If we model realistic utilization shape (70% daytime peak, 30% baseline, 40% average) a blended reserved+burst product with a smaller minimum commit can hit predictable revenue while allowing customers to absorb spikes w/o large overage sticker shock.

Model tabs (walkthrough):
1) Inputs (single column inputs):
   - GPU type: A100-80GB
   - Host list price (cloud-equivalent capex): $3.20/hr (baseline for equivalent on-demand in our market model)
   - Infra overhead multiplier: 1.18 (networking, storage, infra ops)
   - Fixed infra monthly (per cluster) allocate: $1,200
   - Expected life amortization per GPU-month: $1,300 (for capital + maintenance)
   - Target margin (gross) for Dedicated product: 35%
   - Typical customer utilization scenarios: low 25%, med 45%, high 70%
   - Commit term options: 1-month, 3-month, 12-month
   - Burst pool cap: up to 30% of committed capacity for short windows

2) CapacityCalc (how many GPU-hours per month a commit represents):
   - GPU-hours/month = commit_count * 24 * 30 = commit_count * 720
   - Effective cost per GPU-hour (raw) = (amortization + infra monthly allocate/commit_count) / 720 + host_list_price * infra_overhead_multiplier
   - Note: this cell currently uses per-GPU amortization as a proxy; TODO: add zone/instance-family delta and HSM/KMS add-ons.

3) PricingScenarios (three illustrative pricing lattices):
   Scenario A — Steady Commit (baseline):
     - 10 GPU commit, 12-month term, list-equivalent hour = computed raw cost, discount to customer = 28% -> published rate = $2.30/hr
     - Predicted utilization = 55% -> effective cost to customer per used GPU-hour = $4.18/hr (published rate / utiliz) -> note: this demonstrates value when normalized to per-used-hour vs pay-as-you-go
   Scenario B — Small commit + burst credits:
     - 3 GPU commit, 3-month term, base published rate = $2.95/hr, burst pool: up to 30% additional concurrent capacity at 1.6x base rate when used (overage).
     - Use-case: customers with spiky traffic; effective blended utilization and revenue have lower variance; revenue per-month is higher vs flat 3-GPU on-demand at lower utilization assumption because burst capture.
   Scenario C — Flex convertibility (commit buffer):
     - 5 GPU commit with monthly true-up; publish low base $2.60/hr for commit utilization; unused commit credit can roll 1 month. Overage priced at $3.45/hr. Auto-scale policy allowed only into burst pool until 150% of commit.
4) Sensitivity tab (key experiments):
   - Vary host list price ±15% (simulate market infra shifts).
   - Vary utilization assumptions (avg 30% to 80%) and observe breakeven for customer vs hosted API.
   - Vary amortization window (24mo vs 36mo) to see capex impact on per-hour.
   - Experiment: convert burst pool pricing from multiplier to flat per-hour overage to test customer read-understanding.

Example sensitivity result (excerpt):
   - If amortization increases 20% (shorter hardware life), published rate must increase ~9% to maintain 35% margin if utilization remains 50%.
   - For 3 GPU commit: moving from expected utilization 45% -> 60% reduces effective per-used-hour by ~25% in customer-facing economics (big incentive to push better scheduling / caching).

Behavioral experiments / heuristics captured in model: 
   - Prefix caching improvements reduce token hours by ~12% for chat workloads; sensitivity tab has toggles to apply this to expected token throughput which in turn drops effective per-token cost.
   - Workload mix: embedding-heavy workloads have high per-token parallelism but lower seq-len; we model this as lower average GPU-hour consumption per request and allow a separate bucket.

Key findings (working):
   - Smaller commits (1-3 GPUs) with a predictable burst pool marketed as "elastic buffer" are attractive to early-stage customers and lower sales friction. They carry slightly higher revenue volatility but dramatically expand TAM for Dedicated product.
   - 12-month commits remain best for large customers where utilization is sustained; margin delta vs 3-month commit is ~9–12% depending on amortization assumptions.
   - Burst pricing must be simple — customers prefer a small multiplier (1.4x) over weird tiered cents/hour for cognitive simplicity.

Customer-facing constructs recommended (draft):
   - Reserved Lite: monthly commit, 1–5 GPUs, base rate = list*0.78, burst up to 25% at 1.5x base, roll unused credits 1 month.
   - Reserved Standard: 6–50 GPUs, 3-month commit, base rate = list*0.72, burst up to 30% at 1.4x base, can opt for predictable scaling windows.
   - Reserved Enterprise: 50+ GPUs, 12-month commit, negotiable pricing, dedicated billing cadence, SLA credits, on-prem options.

Implementation notes (ops/infra):
   - Need a hard limit in control plane to enforce burst pool caps and billing meter boundaries. Ticket: PRJ-4821 tracks burst enforcement work.
   - Billing: require a new SKU for "burst-hour" with multiplier logic in billing stack — include metadata so console shows easy forecast.
   - Metrics: expose commit utilization % by customer weekly (rolling 7d and 30d) + expected next-month forecast.

Open questions / TODOs (explicit):
   - Validate host_list_price with infra cost team (Marco R).
   - Run cohort analysis on existing Dedicated customers for month-to-month utilization patterns (SRE/analytics).
   - Decide whether overage rounds up to nearest 1 minute or is metered per 30s (affects small-burst economics).
   - Legal: add clause for minimum notice for reducing commit count (30 vs 60 vs 90 days).

Quick simulation snapshots (manual values):
   - 10 GPU commit, 55% utilization, published rate $2.30/hr -> customer monthly bill = 10 * 720 * $2.30 = $16,560; effective per-used-hour = $2.30 / 0.55 = $4.18 -> per-token example (chat, avg 40 tokens/sec for 30s session) = rough bucketed cost ~ $0.000045/token (back-of-envelope).
   - 3 GPU commit + bursts, base $2.95/hr, assume bursts used 8% of month at 1.6x rate -> blended revenue ~ $1,900/mo (example numbers in sheet).

Version notes:
   - This sheet intentionally keeps formulas in plain english cells so reviewers can follow logic without diving into code. When we finalize, port to formal spreadsheet with explicit formula cells and a scenario-dashboard.

Meeting / next steps:
   - Review w/ pricing council: week of Jan 19th.
   - Infra validation (cost inputs) due Jan 22nd.
   - Sales playbook draft to capture positioning for "Reserved Lite" by Feb 2nd.

Notes to self:
   - Keep scenarios simple for GTM; customers get confused by >2 burst shapes.
   - Add a separate micro-bucket for embedding workloads — might allow a lower base rate due to higher hardware efficiency.

End of doc (working).
